text:
incident-bot: PAGER: region=ap-northeast2, service=redwood-serving, symptom=GPU pool saturated + autoscaler stuck. Queue growth 6m, pending requests ~4200, error rate 502s increasing. Possible cause: GCP quota denial for GPUs when attempting scale-up. Paging on-call.

maya (on-call): taking this. seeing the spike in the queue graph. thanks for the ping. starting triage.

alex (eng-runtime): confirmed autoscaler got scale-up failures around 1759998740 with errors: 
```
ERROR: failed to create instance: quotaExceeded for resource type "GPUS" in region ap-northeast2
status: 403
message: Insufficient quota to satisfy request
```
Looks like cluster-autoscaler kept retrying but GCP rejected new nodes.

maya (on-call): steps i will run now: 1) verify quota via gcloud 2) open support ticket if quota is low 3) enable traffic failover to fallback region 4) throttle low-priority tenants to reduce immediate load.

sam (infra): run `gcloud compute regions describe ap-northeast2 --project=redwood-prod` and `gcloud compute project-info describe --project=redwood-prod` to see quota. i can run the quota request if we need a fast lift, but GCP can take time.

maya (on-call): running quota check now:
```
$ gcloud compute regions describe ap-northeast2 --project=redwood-prod --quiet --format=json | jq '.quotas[] | select(.metric=="GPUS")'
{"metric":"GPUS","limit":48.0,"usage":48.0}
```
quota at hard limit (48), usage 48. that's why scale-up fails.

joan (sre-lead): thanks. we can't rely on quota bump to be instant. plan B: failover some traffic to us-west1, and reduce concurrency per-worker to free slots in the pool. also consider turning off burst for non-critical shards.

maya (on-call): executing immediate mitigations:
- set routing policy to prefer us-west1 for new requests (canary 30m)
- decrease max-concurrency on pods serving non-enterprise tenants from 8 -> 4
- pause scheduled batch jobs that consume GPUs

alex (eng-runtime): routing change (edge) command:
```
# update route in frontend-routing service
kubectl -n infra patch configmap/route-policy -p '{"data":{"ap-northeast2-preference":"0.3"}}'
deploy-bot: triggered rollout for edge-proxy (edge-proxy-v12 -> v13)
```

deploy-bot: deployment edge-proxy rolled out: 3/3 ready. :rocket: 

maya (on-call): throttling policy patch (non-critical tenants):
```
kubectl -n serving patch configmap/tenant-priority -p '{"data":{"non_critical_qps_limit":"50"}}'
```
this will shed ~1200 pending requests according to our SLO model.

sam (infra): opened a quota increase request with GCP support (case 12345678). ETA is unpredictable. I also triggered a manual allocation shuffle to see if there are idle GPUs in other projects we can borrow temporarily (internal only).

karen (customer-success): heads up — we're seeing customer-facing 502s. i'll draft a short status note for affected customers and coordinate any urgent contract-sensitive ones.

joan (sre-lead): can we get a short summary for incident timeline and impact? I'll join if we need postmortem.

maya (on-call): short timeline so far:
- 1759998600: background autoscaler began scaling due to traffic increase
- 1759998700: attempts to create new nodes -> GCP quota denial logs start
- 1759998740: autoscaler retries / errors escalate, cluster cannot increase GPU capacity
- 1759998800: queue grows past 3k pending, tail latency spikes, some 502s generated by eviction / timeout
- 1759998888: incident-bot paged on-call
- ongoing: routing pivot and throttles applied, quota request submitted.

alex (eng-runtime): additional quick fixes we applied: lowered per-request tokenization batch size to reduce per-call GPU memory pressure (config blob applied):
```
# serving config change
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 1024  -> 768
  max_batch_items: 8  -> 6
```
should reduce memory footprint enough to squeeze a few extra concurrent slots.

maya (on-call): monitoring impact: pending queue dropped from 4200 -> 2700 after throttles + routing. error rate down 40%. still above acceptable.

sam (infra): update from quota case: GCP replied with acknowledgement, estimating regional quota review in 4-6 hours. flagged as high. meanwhile we can try cross-project borrowing.

karen (customer-success): I've posted an interim update to affected customers: short note + recommended retries. some customers asked for ETA — citing 4-6h for quota is fine but flagging that we'll continue to divert traffic.

joan (sre-lead): good. next: schedule a quick postmortem once we stabilize. include follow-ups: 1) automated cross-region failover rules for GPU-quota hits 2) runbook for quota-denied autoscaler 3) limit-based circuit breaker for non-critical tenants 4) billing/commit adjustments to increase regional baseline.

maya (on-call): one more immediate operational note — if anyone needs to reproduce the autoscaler failure locally, here's the relevant error in the cluster-autoscaler logs (redacted):
```
I0409 17:12:20.123] Scale-up: ignoring request for 3 nodes (max nodes total 48 reached)
I0409 17:12:20.124] Pod "inference-abc" couldn't be scheduled: 1 node(s) didn't match node selector, 48/48 GPUs allocated
E0409 17:12:20.130] failed to create node: googleapi: Error 403: Quota 'GPUS' exceeded for project 123456 by region ap-northeast2., quotaExceeded
```

alex (eng-runtime): please alert me if the routing pivot causes any unexpected model-registry mismatches (model versions pinned regionally). i'll monitor.

maya (on-call): current status: mitigations active, partial recovery. next ticks: keep routing for 30m, watch queue and error rate, if queue < 500 resume normal routing, otherwise prepare escalation to SRE manager for executive comms.

joan (sre-lead): noting action items into post-incident board. thanks all — especially rapid on-call reaction. :clap:

karen (customer-success): i'll follow up with customers in 1h with an update.

deploy-bot: scheduled rollback not triggered. all changes are live and monitored.

maya (on-call): signing off the channel for now, will stay on-call console for next 45m. will update if anything regresses. :headphones:
